item.description:
Rein 0.9.6

  • Virtual Devices now do what the screen says. Activate a device and its sources really feed

it: an app source is copied into the device (the app keeps playing where it was), a microphone

source is passed through into it, and each monitor plays the device's mix on the output you

chose, at the volumes you set — all scaled by the device's master. The L/R meters on the device

card and the meter on every source are live. The status chip on the card tells you exactly what

is running ("Live · 2 sources · 1 monitor") or what's missing ("Publish to system to go live").

  • A real channel map. Publish a device with 4 or more channels and each source picks which

channel pair it lands on — a small patch bay for multi-track recording into one device.

  • Fixed: routing an app to a device that has inputs. Sending an app to a USB interface (or a

Rein device) could copy the interface's *input* back out instead of the app. Rein now finds the

right stream.

  • Extra brightness backs off when the Mac runs hot. Above 90 °C on the hottest sensor the XDR

boost pauses (the slider drops to hardware max and an amber note explains); it comes back below

80 °C and restores where you had it.

  • Housekeeping: "Show in Activity" in Virtual Devices is a working link; the templates now

pre-wire the current mic / output; a placeholder view that no screen used is gone.

Rein 0.9.5

  • App recordings work. Pressing record on an app in Audio → Apps produced an empty, 0-second

file. The audio tap hands Rein one interleaved stereo stream, but the processing chain was written

for a separate left and right buffer and only recorded once it had seen the second one — which

never arrived. Audio is now split into left/right on the way in and rebuilt on the way out, so

recordings (both "as heard" and "raw app audio") capture the whole take.

  • Per-app and System EQ, balance and Audio Unit effects are now truly per-channel. The same

fix means the equalizer no longer runs one filter across both channels' samples (which shifted

its bands upward), balance actually pans instead of turning both channels down, and a hosted

Audio Unit effect is now applied rather than skipped.

  • Virtual Devices copy is honest. With no devices configured the banner explains that the

default stereo "Rein Audio" loopback is what other apps see, and the button says what it does

(reset the system device) instead of "Publish 1".

Rein 0.9.4

  • System EQ is back. A macOS update had silently broken the system-wide equalizer (the audio

tap it relied on started returning silence). The EQ now captures the system mix the same proven

way per-app audio does, so shaping your whole output works again. If an app starts playing while

the EQ is on, it joins within a second.

  • Licence-clean ffmpeg. The bundled ffmpeg is now our own LGPL build — hardware VideoToolbox

H.264 encoding (which casting already used) and native decoders, with the licence text and source

reference shipped in the app. No user-visible change to casting; very old HDR films may tone-map

with slightly simpler colour handling.
